doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: The King Oliver band lineup and the Savoy and Cotton Club episode
summary: Paul lists the personnel in Oliver's New York band and describes its failure after Oliver refused the Cotton Club job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well we went with King Oliver. Let's see, I think I can remember some of the names in that band. It was pretty long ways back. But on trumpet there, they had King Oliver. They had a trumpet player called Gray. So far I can't remember his name. He was Gray and Red Allen. It was three trumpets. On trombone we had one, we had Kid Ory on trombone. Now on bass we had a fellow, but his name was Buford. That's all I can remember. Buford, heavy dog. Buford, he was a bass player. On saxophone we had Omar Simeon. I think he passed away.
Just a week and a half ago.
And Bonnie Bigard and myself. They had rumors that we were the best sax section in New York at that time.
You went on to New York band with them? With that section.

And on the percussion we had on piano, Louis Russell and Paul Barbaran on drums. But the band didn't have any success. We stayed there and we worked at the Savoy Ballroom. We had no more than about two weeks and whatever came up, King Oliver came out. He didn't seem, he could get enough money. So he had offered to go to the cotton club and that was his great mistake. He wouldn't accept it. And that was King Oliver's downfall. Because he didn't think there was enough money in it and he wouldn't accept it. So Duke Ellington accepted the job. And the Duke Ellington band was broke up at that time and he was putting men together. He had Otto, a fellow on saxophone, and he was in need of saxophone players so he got the big odd from King Oliver's band, because our band was split up around New York. So he got the big odd to play saxophone.
